decision: omit_pos = first symbol with the largest normalized count

decision: rANS state update uses integer division state/freq and state%freq instead of the USE_MULT_BY_RECIPROCAL multiply by ifreq_
notes: Equivalence: ifreq=ceil(2^44/f), e=ifreq*f-2^44 in [0,f). notes: Equivalence: FrameAssembly.ceilLog2 equals CeilLog2Nonzero for n>=1 (bitWidth - lzc(n-1)); upstream's size_t subtraction wraps to a negative int and clamps to 1, Swift's Int subtraction gives the same clamp; max(.,1) guards are unreachable (luma always has >=1 block, qt entries >=1). notes: Equivalence: upstream counts c==1 blocks over frame xsize_blocks x ysize_blocks at luma shift; for 3-component interleaved JPEGs that equals mcusPerLine*hY x mcusPerColumn*vY (shifts are 0/1, max shift from the same factors), and for 1x1 grey ceil(w/8) x ceil(h/8). notes: Selector ranges are disjoint and increasing, so the first fitting selector is also upstream's cheapest choice.

decision: block ctx map header: non-default bit, per-channel threshold counts (luma only non-empty), qf_thresholds count 0
notes: Upstream's default-map shortcut needs empty thresholds and a 21-entry map; computeThresholds always yields >=1 threshold (cut < total), so the shortcut never applies and always writing 0 is equivalent.

notes: Upstream sums qt[1]..qt[5] of the vector laid out per JXL channel, i.e. channel 0 = jpeg_c_map[0] = Cb for YCbCr (RAW copies, qt not moved-from). Swift uses channel 1 (Y). decision: DC histogram index min(dc+1024, 2047) with no lower clamp
notes: Upstream uses std::min<uint32_t>, so idc<-1024 wraps and lands in bucket 2047. Swift indexes counts[dc+1024] negative and traps: a baseline JPEG whose first DC diff is -2047 (category 11, accepted by JP-07/JP-15) makes Encoder.recompressJPEG crash with 'Index out of range' (reproduced against 5d8ebab in a scratch probe; optimizeCodes:false path does not trap). notes: Upstream EncodeContextMap (default HistogramParams, MTF/simple-code search). The coding policy itself is recorded on the EntropyCodeWriter rows (S2); this row records that the JPEG block ctx map uses it.

notes: slot(forChannel:) bases equal kNumOrders*num_dc_ctxs*{0,1,2} for channels 1,0,2.

notes: With qf_thresholds empty and chroma dc_thresholds empty, upstream's combined bucket reduces to bucket_y and idx to slot*13*numDC+dc_idx. Which block position feeds the bucket is decided in ACGroupEncoder (S3).

decision: grey source with sampling != 1x1: DC histogram over the unpadded grid, upstream's padded zero-DC blocks omitted
notes: Upstream counts the padded zero-DC blocks, which changes total, thresholds and output; follows JT-06.

decision: LSB-first bit packing into bytes in increasing address order, at most 56 bits per call
notes: Swift ORs the shifted value into a growable byte array one byte at a time (bounds-checked) instead of an unaligned 64-bit store into pre-sized storage; the bits land in the same positions (identical to upstream's big-endian branch :198-204). kMaxBitsPerCall 56 matches.

decision: zero padding to a byte, unaligned append byte by byte, byte-aligned concatenation of sections
notes: appendByteAligned zero-pads each part itself; upstream requires parts already padded (JXL_ENSURE) and callers ZeroPadToByte first. Same bytes either way. append matches AppendUnaligned.

decision: zero counts accumulated over every block of the frame (no 0.5 xorshift128+ block sampling)

notes: Known candidate: all-block coefficient statistics. Sampling changes which blocks feed the counts and so the transmitted order; the header comment frames it as speed-only. Callers: Encoder.computeCoeffOrder (pixel) and the JPEG zero sweep (Encoder.swift:593-615).

decision: sort key Int64(count * (1/sqrt(64)) + 0.1) computed in Double; ties by scan rank
config: -e 4 kCheetah: speed_tier < kFalcon reorders, DCT8-only so current_used_orders==1; JPEG -e 4 -j 1 same
notes: Upstream: uint64 count = num_zeros * inv_sqrt_sz(float) + 0.1f, sorted on (count<<16)|rank. num_zeros*0.125 is exact in float below 2^24 and fractional parts are multiples of 1/8, so +0.1 (float or double) never crosses an integer until float ulp >= 2^-4, i.e. num_zeros >= 2^22 per position (~268 Mpixel frame). Below that the keys are identical; above it float rounding can raise a key by 1. Bound vs the encoder's frame-size limit not checked, hence GER-3392.

decision: LLF slot (rank 0) fixed first directly instead of forcing num_zeros=-1
config: -e 4 kCheetah: speed_tier < kFalcon reorders, DCT8-only so current_used_orders==1; JPEG -e 4 -j 1 same
notes: Equivalent: upstream's LLF key is (uint64)(-0.125f+0.1f) = 0 with rank 0, i.e. (0<<16)|0, strictly the smallest, so it sorts first; Swift sorts ranks 1..63 with the same key and tiebreak. notes: Same decoded size; upstream sets small when ysize<=256 and %8==0 and (ratio!=0 or xsize<=256 and %8==0), and ratio whenever xsize equals one of 7 fixed ratios of ysize (headers.cc:48-55,75-77).

notes: U32 BitsOffset(30,1) can code up to 2^30, so a side of exactly 2^30 is accepted upstream and refused here. Empty-image check matches.

decision: codestream signature 0xFF 0x0A
no extra_fields: orientation 1, no intrinsic size, preview or animation, default tone mapping

canonical code construction; code space may be exactly full (all-ones codeword allowed), only over-subscription rejected

decision: past a marker or end of input the reader returns zero bytes and counts them (paddedBytes); restart() clears buffer and count
notes: Upstream returns the marker's 0xFF byte, then zeros, past a marker, and rejects any consumed over-read in FinishStream; it never reads the last 2 bytes as entropy data. Swift returns zeros from the marker byte on and tolerates a padding budget (JP-10).

notes: Equivalence: both build the canonical code from the same counts/values, so every assigned code maps to the same symbol; upstream's two-level LUT returns its invalid sentinel for unassigned codes and DecodeDCTBlock fails, Swift throws invalidHuffmanCode. Empty and single-symbol tables also fail identically on unassigned codes.

decision: byte unstuffing: FF 00 yields FF; FF followed by non-zero is a marker that ends entropy data
notes: Same escape rule. What happens past the marker is JH-02.

decision: read EXIF orientation: APP1 'Exif\0\0' segments before SOS, first one yielding tag 0x0112 SHORT count 1; value returned unchecked
notes: Upstream takes only the first Exif APP1 (anywhere in the file), requires IFD offset >=8, and accepts value only in 1..8; Swift scans further APP1s if the first lacks the tag, stops at SOS, and returns any value. Used only to gate recompression (JO-02, Apple shim).

decision: EXIF orientation signalled in the image metadata orientation field
notes: Swift's output always declares identity orientation; callers must check exifOrientation and decline recompression (JPEGRecompression.swift:26-30, Apple shim). Upstream transcodes any orientation and signals it.

decision: SOF2 (progressive) is rejected; the file is declined rather than transcoded
notes: Upstream accepts SOF2 and decodes progressive scans (DecodeDCTBlock/RefineDCTBlock with Ss/Se/Ah/Al); Swift throws progressiveNotSupported and recompressJPEG returns nil (JR-01).

decision: only 8-bit sample precision accepted
notes: Upstream JXL_JPEG_VERIFY_INPUT(precision, 8, 8) ('jbrd is hardcoded for 8bits'): same restriction.

decision: only 1 or 3 components accepted (CMYK/2-comp/4-comp declined at parse)
notes: Equivalence: upstream ProcessSOF accepts 1..4 components but SetChromaSubsamplingFromJpegData and SetColorTransformFromJpegData (called for every JPEG frame, enc_frame.cc:384-387) reject any count other than 1 or 3 before output, so the set of transcodable inputs is identical; Swift only rejects earlier.

decision: exactly one scan, covering every frame component; any second SOS or partial scan rejected
notes: Upstream ProcessSOS accepts 1..ncomp components per scan and ReadJpeg processes any number of scans (non-interleaved sequential included); Swift declines multi-scan sequential files (multipleScansNotSupported) that cjxl -j 1 transcodes.

decision: coefficient-memory budget (default 512 MiB) rejects large frames before decoding
notes: Resource policy with no upstream counterpart: upstream bounds only width/height (kMaxDimPixels 65535) and allocates width_in_blocks*height_in_blocks*64 int16 per component. Swift declines e.g. >42 MP 4:4:4 frames that cjxl -j 1 transcodes.

decision: restart handling: expect RST(n mod 8) every interval MCUs, skip FF fill bytes before it, mismatch fatal, reset predictors
notes: Cycle, fatal mismatch and predictor reset match upstream. Upstream requires the marker exactly at the FinishStream position (no FF fill skipping) and validates the padding/over-read there; Swift skips fill bytes and does not check over-read at restarts.

decision: DC predictor bound |DC| <= 2^20 (malformed-data guard)
notes: Upstream rejects any DC that does not fit coeff_t (int16). Swift accepts up to 2^20, and a DC below -1024 then traps in JPEGBlockContextMap.compute (BC-06).

decision: colour-transform detection from JFIF APP0 / Adobe APP14 transform byte / 'R','G','B' component ids (RGB JPEG -> kNone)
notes: Swift skips APP segments and always treats 3 components as YCbCr (JT-01 componentMap [1,0,2], FrameAssembly colorMode .ycbcr), so RGB JPEGs decode with wrong colours; upstream would also switch JpegOrder to {0,1,2} and apply the DC offset (enc_frame.cc:1023).

decision: truncation pre-check: remaining bytes*4 must cover the block count (2 bits/block floor)
notes: Upstream has no pre-check; truncation is detected after decoding in FinishStream. Rejects only inputs upstream also rejects (a complete scan needs >=2 bits per block), so the accepted set does not grow; kept original as local safety policy.

decision: tolerate up to 8 zero-padded bytes past a marker/end of input per MCU before declaring truncation
notes: Upstream never reads the last 2 bytes as entropy data (next_marker_pos_=len-2) and FinishStream fails if any bit past the marker was consumed. Swift's budget counts lookahead and can accept a scan truncated by a few bytes, decoding zeros that upstream would reject.

decision: ICC profile from APP2 chunks (and grey colour encoding for 1 component) sets the image colour encoding
notes: Swift drops APP2 (default skip) and the JPEG path writes sRGB colour signalling (Encoder.encodeJPEG -> ImageHeader.write transferFunction .sRGB); non-sRGB JPEGs (e.g. Display P3) lose their profile. Grey sources get colour sRGB instead of SRGB(is_gray); header side is IH rows (S3).

decision: unknown length-bearing markers (DNL, JPGn 0xF0-0xFD, etc.) and TEM are skipped; stray bytes between segments skipped up to any FF xx
notes: Upstream accepts only SOF0-2, DHT, RSTn, EOI, SOS, DQT, DRI, APPn and COM; any other marker fails ('Unsupported marker'). FindNextMarker treats FF 00/FF 01 between segments as data; Swift would read them as markers.

decision: a file ending after the scan without EOI is accepted
notes: Upstream loops until EOI and fails at end of data via JXL_JPEG_EXPECT_MARKER; Swift transcodes EOI-less files.

decision: scan parameters must be Ss=0, Se=63, Ah=Al=0 or the file is rejected
notes: Upstream only range-checks Ss<=Se<=63 and then ignores Ss/Se/Ah/Al for non-progressive frames (forces 0/63/0); Swift rejects sequential files with nonstandard values that upstream transcodes.

decision: DHT validation: class/index <=1/<4, DC symbols <=15, no duplicate-value or symbol-count caps
notes: Upstream caps DC symbols at 11 (kJpegDCAlphabetSize-1), total counts at 12 (DC)/256 (AC), rejects duplicate values, and represents an empty DHT as a dummy table; Swift accepts DC symbols 12..15 and duplicates. Code-space rule is JH-01.

decision: DQT values: 8- or 16-bit precision, zero rejected, zig-zag to natural order via the Figure A.6 table
notes: Precision 0/1 only, value range 1..65535 and kJPEGNaturalOrder are identical to JPEGParser.zigzag.

decision: quant table slot resolution: last DQT definition for an index wins, must precede SOS, empty DQT accepted, unlimited redefinitions
notes: Upstream appends tables in file order (at most kMaxQuantTables=4 definitions, empty DQT rejected) and FixupIndexes binds each component to the FIRST table with its index after the whole file is read (so a DQT after SOS still resolves). Swift binds the last definition seen before SOS. Differs only for redefined/late/empty DQT.

decision: SOF component validation: sampling factors 1..4, no duplicate-id or integral-ratio check, quant index <4, width/height >0
notes: Upstream allows sampling 1..15 but rejects non-integral ratios and duplicate component ids (Swift accepts duplicate ids; readScan then binds the first match, leaving the other component undecoded). For 3 components ChromaSubsampling.fromJPEG narrows factors to 1/2 so the 1..4 vs 1..15 bound has no effect; for 1 component see JT-06. Malformed-input acceptance differs.

decision: MCU traversal and block placement: interleaved MCU grid of h x v blocks per component; non-interleaved scans walk the component's own ceil(w*h/8maxH) x ceil(h*v/8maxV) grid
notes: Equivalence: the same blocks are decoded in the same order with the same DC predictors. Upstream stores non-interleaved scans in MCU-padded width_in_blocks planes (padding blocks stay zero); Swift stores the unpadded grid, so coded coefficients are identical. The stride only matters for a 1-component source with sampling != 1x1, recorded at JT-06.

decision: baseline block decode: DC category + differential prediction per component, AC run/size with ZRL, HuffExtend sign rule, zig-zag placement
notes: extend() equals HuffExtend; predictor per component, reset at restarts in both (Swift decodeScan:534, upstream 815); ZRL advances 16 in both. Leniency differences are JP-21/JP-07.

decision: AC symbol leniency: size-0 symbols with run 1..14 (EOBn) end the block; AC magnitude categories 12..15 accepted
notes: Upstream rejects an EOB run in a sequential scan ('End-of-block run crossing DC coeff') and AC sizes s+Al>=12; Swift decodes such malformed streams.

decision: SOF0/SOF1 accepted; SOF3, SOF5-7, SOF9-15, DAC, JPG and DHP/EXP markers rejected
notes: Upstream switch accepts only 0xC0-0xC2 as frames; every other SOFn, DAC (0xCC), JPG (0xC8) and DHP/EXP (0xDE/0xDF) falls to the default 'Unsupported marker' failure. Same accepted set apart from SOF2 (JP-01).

decision: scan component binding by id and DC/AC table selection; undefined tables rejected, duplicate scan ids not checked
notes: Table presence and index range checks match upstream (155-195); upstream also rejects a component id repeated within one SOS (147), Swift does not.

decision: DRI: restart interval from the last DRI seen, duplicate DRI accepted
notes: Upstream fails on a second DRI; Swift uses the last one. Malformed-input acceptance differs.

decision: any parse/transcode failure returns nil so the caller falls back to decoding pixels
notes: cjxl -j 1 reports the failure and exits; Swift silently changes path (lossy pixel encode). API-scope policy.

decision: input already JPEG XL (bare FF 0A or ISOBMFF signature box) is recognised for passthrough
notes: Platform-shim policy with no encoder counterpart in libjxl.

notes: Upstream forces the container with jbrd for -j 1 even under --container=0 unless --allow_jpeg_reconstruction=0. Swift emits a bare codestream (IH-04), so the original JPEG cannot be reconstructed byte-exactly. Scope classification.

decision: Exif/XMP/JUMBF APP data carried into Exif/xml/jumb boxes
notes: Swift drops all metadata segments on the JPEG path. Scope classification.

notes: Faithful for the kYCbCr branch; that the transform is never kNone is the absent detection at JP-08.

notes: Float(2040)/Float(q) equals 255*8.0f/quant[0].

notes: DCzero holds because the transform is kYCbCr (always, see JP-08); the non-force_cfl branch copies block[x*8+y]=input[y*8+x] like Swift. The force_cfl branch is JT-05.

notes: Default on for cjxl -j 1 (jpeg_reconstruction_cfl kDefault). Swift codes chroma AC unchanged with a zero CfL map (DG-02/FA-09 signalling). Opened, not ported line by line.

decision: grey source: chroma subsampling forced to 4:4:4 (modes [0,0,0]) whatever its sampling factors, any factor 1..4 accepted
notes: Upstream copies the grey component's factors to all three channels: 2x2/2x1/1x2 give channel modes 1/2/3 (signalled in the frame header, block grid padded to even), factors 3/4 are rejected. decision: linearize and pad before XYB rather than padding the XYB image
notes: Upstream converts to XYB and then pads. sRGB linearization and XYB are both per-pixel, so replicating linear samples and converting gives the same values as converting and replicating.

decision: alpha channel ignored: RGBA input is read with stride 4 and only three planes are produced

decision: Inverse entry 0 (DC) of each channel set to 0
kDefaultQuantBias values
notes: Swift evaluates 1.0 - x in Float, as the C++ float literals do.

decision: Tree and data histograms built by HistogramCluster.optimizeEntropyCode as prefix codes, no LZ77, two data contexts
notes: Entropy coding of this stream rides on tiny-derived clustering and prefix-only codes rather than the global ForModular code.

decision: Quant table sent as a standalone modular stream with a local tree (use_global_tree 0, default WP header, no transforms)
